# Requirements

Deus today carries three payment rails it owns end-to-end — direct (per-call PAX transfer via the embedded wallet, gas every call), net (deus-owned pairwise channels + EIP-712 vouchers + own settler + PaymentChannel.sol, the audit's HIGH-finding cluster), and stream (PaymentStreams precompile sessions). LayerX exists precisely as the generalization of the net rail (layerx/DESIGN.md: 'Deus marketplace — a purchase is just a layerx_pay between two DIDs'). This feature deletes all three rails and re-platforms deus as a LayerX application: every payment is USDX between DIDs on the LayerX ledger, authorized in-band over HTTP by LXP — a challenge/response handshake with the interaction shape of Coinbase's x402 but none of its protocol (no EIP-3009, no USDC, no per-call gas, no third-party facilitator). An unpaid request gets HTTP 402 with an lxp/1 terms body carrying a prefetched LayerX challenge nonce; the payer signs the standard LayerX ed25519 intent preimage with its DID key and retries with X-LayerX-Payment; the server submits the intent to layerxd (invariant i6: the signature IS the authorization, the transporter is irrelevant), executes, and responds with X-LayerX-Receipt. LayerX gains one structural primitive — holds (authorize -> capture/release with payer-authorized captor_did) — plus a ref binding field on intents, so deus keeps its reserve/finalize/void safety while never custodying a micro-USDX. Locked decisions (Andrew 2026-07-13): HTTP 402 status with lxp body/headers; USDX-native pricing replaces wei/PAX; payer-authorized captor_did; stream rail deleted outright; middleware kit (Go + Node) in v1 scope; ref row-level v1 with the leaf-domain bump deferred. Deletion lands LAST, only after the end-to-end no-fakes proofs are green on the new path.

## Requirement 1: LayerX holds: authorize -> capture/release as a ledger primitive

**User Story:** As a paying agent, I want funds reserved inside my own account until the service delivers, so that pay-only-on-success holds without anyone custodying my money.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a valid DID-signed hold intent (canonical preimage over to_did, amount, ttl_s, ref, captor_did per auth.IntentMessage) is accepted, THE ledger SHALL atomically debit the payer's spendable balance_usdx into an open hold row (payer, payee, captor, amount, expiry, ref), such that held funds are unspendable by pay and withdraw.
2. WHEN the captor captures amount <= held before expiry, THE ledger SHALL consume the hold and credit the payee by emitting a STANDARD transfer (monotonic seq, Merkle leaf, sequencer signature) through the same store/accumulator path as Pay, returning any remainder to the payer's balance in the same transaction.
3. WHEN a hold is released (by captor or payer) or expires, THE full held amount SHALL return to the payer's balance; the settle worker SHALL sweep expired holds within one tick; hold, capture, and release SHALL be idempotent.
4. THE supply/reserve proof SHALL count open holds as circulating (circulating = sum(balance_usdx) + sum(open holds)), and a property test SHALL prove the reserve invariant and value conservation across arbitrary interleavings of hold/capture/release/pay/withdraw.

## Requirement 2: ref binding on intents and receipts (row-level v1)

**User Story:** As a marketplace, I want each payment cryptographically bound to the invocation it pays for, so that paid-vs-served disputes are decidable from signed artifacts.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. PAY and HOLD intents SHALL accept an optional ref (0x + 64 hex); WHEN present it SHALL be part of the payer-signed canonical preimage, making the binding provable by the payer's own ed25519 signature.
2. THE ref SHALL be stored on the transfer row (and hold row) and returned in receipt JSON including the public GET /v1/receipt/{seq} and explorer transfer views; folding ref into the leaf preimage (domain bump) is explicitly deferred to v2.
3. A test SHALL prove a ref-carrying pay round-trips intent -> transfer row -> public receipt, and that a tampered ref fails intent signature verification.

## Requirement 3: Hold HTTP surface on layerxd

**User Story:** As a resource server, I want hold lifecycle over plain HTTP with the existing LayerX auth model, so that any service can reserve/capture without new trust assumptions.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. POST /v1/hold SHALL accept a DID-signed intent or X-LayerX-Agent principal token (the writeCaller pattern), returning hold_id + a hold record; insufficient spendable balance SHALL return 402 insufficient_funds in parity with /v1/pay.
2. POST /v1/hold/{id}/capture SHALL be authorized ONLY as the hold's captor_did (principal token or signed capture intent over hold_id + amount), enforcing amount, fixed payee, and expiry bounds; a capture response SHALL carry the emitted transfer receipt.
3. POST /v1/hold/{id}/release SHALL be authorized as captor or payer; GET /v1/hold/{id} SHALL be a public read; write endpoints SHALL sit behind the existing write rate-limit class.
4. REAL HTTP tests over the real store SHALL cover the full lifecycle, captor-authorization rejections, expiry, and double-capture rejection.

## Requirement 4: LXP challenge/response wire protocol

**User Story:** As a paying agent, I want payment terms and settlement to ride the HTTP exchange itself, so that discovering, paying for, and calling a service is one flow with no accounts or api keys.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a priced resource is requested without X-LayerX-Payment, THE server SHALL respond HTTP 402 with an lxp/1 JSON terms object: protocol, asset (USDX), amount_usdx (normalized 6dp), pay_to (payee DID), mode (exact|hold), nonce (a LayerX challenge prefetched for the payer's DID), ref, layerx (base URL), expires_at (<= nonce TTL), and optional quote_id — plus captor_did and ttl_s when mode=hold.
2. WHEN the request retries with X-LayerX-Payment (base64url JSON: from_did, public_key, nonce, signature, to_did, amount_usdx, mode, ref), THE server SHALL verify shape, submit the intent to layerxd, execute the resource, and respond 200 with X-LayerX-Receipt (base64url JSON: seq, leaf_hash, sequencer_sig, amount_usdx, ref).
3. AN invalid, expired, replayed, or underfunded payment SHALL yield a fresh 402 challenge (new nonce) with a machine-readable reason — never execution; WHEN layerxd is unreachable THE server SHALL respond 503 payment_unavailable — never a free call.
4. REPLAY of a settled request (same idempotency key + payment) SHALL return the stored result without a second charge.

## Requirement 5: deus internal/layerx client

**User Story:** As the deus gateway, I want a typed client for layerxd, so that challenge prefetch, settlement, holds, and receipt reads are one seam.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. AN internal/layerx package SHALL wrap challenge prefetch, pay, hold, capture, release, receipt fetch, and account read against DEUS_LAYERX_URL (+ optional transport bearer), mapping layerxd error codes to typed errors (insufficient_funds, unauthorized, unavailable).
2. THE gateway SHALL authenticate to layerxd as its own DID (ed25519 key at DEUS_LXP_KEY) for captor operations, via the existing challenge/verify principal-token lane.
3. REAL httptest round-trip tests SHALL run against the real layerxd HTTP handler.

## Requirement 6: Gateway re-platform: the LXP rail replaces wallet/channels/streams

**User Story:** As the marketplace operator, I want invoke to meter and settle exclusively through LayerX, so that the stubbed wallet and evidence-only channel rails can be deleted.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. BEHIND DEUS_RAIL_LAYERX, Invoke SHALL run the LXP flow: exact mode executes then submits the pay (preserving the current direct-rail ordering and void-on-failure semantics); hold mode reserves via hold, executes, captures on success and releases on failure — replacing wallet.AuthorizeSpend/Send, channels.Reserve, and vouchers.BuildPending.
2. THE metering ledger SHALL remain the idempotency/replay spine, gaining layerx_seq and hold_id columns and rail value layerx; Reserve/Finalize/Void semantics map onto hold/capture/release.
3. THE signed execution receipt SHALL gain the LayerX seq and ref, so the payment receipt and execution receipt are cross-bound (paid <-> served) for the same call.
4. POST /v1/quote/{id} SHALL remain for pre-flight discovery, and the 402 challenge SHALL carry equivalent terms so the quote round-trip is optional.

## Requirement 7: USDX-native pricing

**User Story:** As a developer, I want to price my service in USD terms, so that my prices carry no PAX volatility and match how LayerX settles.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. PRICING plans, quotes, and charges SHALL be denominated in micro-USDX (6dp): pricingmath SHALL gain USDX parse/format/charge operations, and the manifest schema SHALL accept unit_price_usdx / min_charge_usdx.
2. QUOTE responses and LXP challenge terms SHALL carry USDX amounts; no wei/PAX amount SHALL appear on any LayerX-rail pay path.
3. A forward-only migration SHALL convert existing pricing rows and repo fixtures; validation SHALL reject wei-priced manifests once the flag is on.

## Requirement 8: Payee DIDs and explorer-backed earnings

**User Story:** As a developer or a listed agent, I want to be paid to my DID instantly in USDX, so that earnings need no deus payout machinery and remain 100% mine.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. SERVICE manifests and developer records SHALL carry payee_did (validated did:matrix shape); registration of a priced service SHALL require it.
2. EVERY LXP settlement SHALL pay the service's payee_did directly on LayerX; deus SHALL never sit in the money path.
3. /v1/me/earnings SHALL join deus invocations with LayerX reads (GET /v1/account/{did}, transfers), and withdrawal SHALL be a link-out to the existing LayerX /v1/withdraw — no deus custody or payout code.

## Requirement 9: deus.mjs client handshake under a spend leash

**User Story:** As an agent, I want payments handled invisibly under my owner's leash when I call marketplace tools, so that using a paid service is just calling a tool.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a tool call receives an lxp 402 challenge, deus.mjs SHALL enforce the daemon-side leash (LAYERX_MAX_SPEND_USDX per call, LAYERX_MAX_DAILY_USDX rolling daily) BEFORE signing; within leash it signs the canonical intent with executor.key and retries once; over leash it surfaces the terms to the agent and SHALL NOT sign.
2. SETTLED calls SHALL surface the LayerX receipt (seq + amount) in the tool result; insufficient-funds challenges SHALL surface deposit guidance (vault address + did_claim path).
3. THE signing preimage SHALL be byte-identical to layerxd's auth.IntentMessage (lockstep with tools/layerx/layerx.mjs), proven by a cross-implementation test vector.

## Requirement 10: LXP middleware kit (v1 scope)

**User Story:** As any service developer, I want a drop-in paywall speaking LXP, so that I can charge for my endpoint without the deus gateway in my data path.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A Go package (deus/pkg/lxp) SHALL expose net/http middleware: price configuration, challenge minting (nonce prefetch via layerxd), payment verification + settlement submit, and the receipt response header — usable by any Go service standalone.
2. A Node middleware (runner harness package) SHALL implement the same lxp/1 protocol for hosted and self-hosted JS services, verified against the same test vectors.
3. THE deus gateway SHALL consume pkg/lxp itself (one implementation, dogfooded).
4. docs/08-payments-billing.md SHALL be rewritten as the LXP protocol spec (wire format, modes, error codes, examples), and the kit SHALL ship a README.

## Requirement 11: The deletion: rails, channels, settlement, wallet, streams, contracts

**User Story:** As the maintainer, I want the superseded payment machinery gone, so that the audit's HIGH-finding surface no longer exists to maintain or trust.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. internal/channels, internal/settlement, internal/wallet, internal/streams, contracts/PaymentChannel.sol, the direct/net/stream rails, and routes /v1/channels, /v1/vouchers/cosign, /v1/streams*, /internal/settle/run SHALL be removed; deus SHALL build green with all remaining tests passing.
2. docs and README SHALL reflect the LayerX-native architecture with no dangling references to deleted rails (repo grep clean of channel/voucher/stream rail symbols outside history/spec).
3. A forward-only migration SHALL retire channel/voucher/stream tables (data preserved, code paths dropped); DEUS_RAIL_LAYERX flag SHALL be removed with LXP as the only rail.
4. THE deletion SHALL land only after the end-to-end proofs (req.12) are green — enforced by task dependency.

## Requirement 12: No-fakes end-to-end proof

**User Story:** As the owner, I want the full economic loop proven on real components before the old rails die, so that the cutover is demonstrated, not asserted.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. AN E2E test SHALL drive real deus gateway + real layerxd handler over the real store through the full loop — 402 challenge -> client signs -> settle -> execute -> 200 + receipts — in BOTH exact and hold modes, verifying cross-bound receipts (shared ref, layerx_seq on the execution receipt) and idempotent replay without double charge.
2. CUSTODY/TRUST properties SHALL be proven: the deus gateway DID's LayerX balance never changes across settlements; capture over amount, past expiry, wrong payee, or by a non-captor is rejected; expired holds release; layerxd-down yields 503 with zero executions.
3. NO test in this feature SHALL substitute a fake for a real code path: real Postgres-backed layerxd, real ed25519 signatures, real HTTP, real gateway pipeline.
